children.value: > Fact From Story: The agency accused Amazon of wielding its monopoly power to squeeze merchants and thwart rivals.

> > Fact From Story: The agency said Amazon punishes third-party sellers who offer cheaper products elsewhere by threatening to disqualify them from appearing in the buy box if it detects a lower price.
> > > Fact From Story: Losing the buy box is an “existential threat” to sellers’ businesses, the complaint alleges.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies generally do not want an existential threat to their business.
> > Fact From Story: The FTC said Amazon relies on an “anti-discounting strategy” and a “massive web-crawling apparatus that constantly tracks online prices” to stifle competition.

> > > Fact From Story: The company steadily hikes the fees it charges sellers and prevents them from discounting on other sites, so sellers often inflate their prices off of Amazon, creating an “artificial price floor everywhere,” according to the complaint.
> > > Fact From Story: For consumers, that’s led to artificially inflated prices and a degraded shopping experience, the agency alleges.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Artificially inflated prices and a degraded shopping experience are harmful to consumers.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Anti-discounting strategies and web-crawling are ways to control prices and stifle competition.
> Commonsense Knowledge: Monopolies are illegal and anti-competitive.
